transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE); Samira Patel (Redwood SE); Leo Chen (Redwood CSM); Maya Singh (Peregrine Head of AI); Carlos Rivera (Peregrine Platform); Anita Bose (Peregrine Security)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining the qbr uh we'll do a quick run through usage, costs, reliability and then roadmap. hey maya carlos, how are you?
[00:06] Maya: hey jordan, doing well thanks, lots going on this quarter so excited to sync.
[00:09] Carlos: yep, thanks. we've got a couple of infra folks on the call today to talk usage patterns.
[00:13] Jordan: great. quick agenda: 1) usage and cost trends 2) incidents / sros 3) pilot / dedicated questions 4) next steps. sound good?
[00:19] Maya: yup
[00:20] Samira: yep, i'll jump into the numbers then. so overall token usage is up about 3.1x q/q, big driver is the new conversational feature rolled into search, average prompt length increased from ~60 tokens to ~130 tokens. we're seeing more long context requests which impacts KV cache utilization and also increases per-token cost.
[00:38] Carlos: when you say KV cache, is that the prefix caching? we noticed some cache misses; curious if that's on our side.
[00:43] Samira: yeah, so the runtime does prefix / KV cache, sometimes per-tenant caching is suboptimal if prompts aren't consistent. we've seen a miss rate spike during the week of black friday where user queries varied a lot. some of the transcripts may show K V cash in the logs, ha, the speech to text got it wrong.
[00:56] Maya: ha, yeah. the big concern is cost — our bill jumped 2.6x and the CFO is asking about options.
[01:02] Jordan: totally expected, given the usage. a few levers: 1) batching and adaptive batching (reduce per-token price with minimal latency impact for async flows) 2) quantized model variants for lower-cost paths 3) reserved dedicated capacity where you get committed throughput pricing.
[01:20] Carlos: can you remind us on committed pricing math vs pay-as-you-go? last time numbers were a bit fuzzy.
[01:24] Jordan: yes — i'll send an updated pricing deck after the call. high level: dedicated reserved capacity gives you ~30-45% cost savings at our standard utilization assumptions versus hosted, depends on batchability and 99th p latency requirements. i'll include several example tiers for your traffic shape.
[01:38] Maya: what's the tradeoff on latency? our search use-case needs sub-300ms 95th p.
[01:43] Samira: hosted with high priority plans can do that for shorter contexts; dedicated with pinned nodes and optimized kernels typically gives more consistent 95/99 p, but you need to tune batch sizes and pre-warming to hit 300ms. also quantization can introduce small upticks in latency but saves cost.
[01:57] Carlos: any example numbers you can share? 95th p and 99th p for dedicated vs hosted for 150 token prompts?
[02:03] Samira: rough numbers from our benchmarks: hosted API 95th ~220ms, 99th ~520ms for that profile; dedicated tuned nodes 95th ~190ms, 99th ~360ms. caveat — depends on hardware type and concurrency. we'll run a dedicated benchmark for your exact model/profile.
[02:19] Maya: that 99th for hosted seems high for us; is that due to autoscaling cold starts?
[02:23] Samira: yes partly autoscale and queuing during spikes. also prefix cache warmness matters. dedicated avoids autoscale variability.
[02:29] Jordan: on reliability, leo, can you give the quick summary of the incidents this quarter?
[02:33] Leo: sure. two notable blips: 1) a 45-minute regional latency increase on 2026-11-05 due to a storage backend degrade that impacted model loading; 2) a 12-minute routing flap during a deploy that caused elevated 500s for a small subset. both were mitigated with fallback to secondary model variants and redeploys. post-mortems shared in the console; i've pasted the links to the incident notes in the notes area.
[02:58] Anita: from security side we need details on encryption at rest and KMS integration if we go dedicated/private. also SOC 2 artifacts — we have an audit next quarter and need evidence for data residency and access logs.
[03:09] Jordan: we have SOC 2 Type II, can share the report, and dedicated/private options integrate with customer KMS and HSM for key management. we'll include the SSO/SAML metadata and the list of audit logs exported to your SIEM.
[03:20] Anita: good. also need VPC peering options and whether logs cross region.
[03:24] Samira: VPC peering and private endpoints are supported; you can pin region and we support audit log export to S3/CloudWatch. region replication only happens if you enable cross-region backups.
[03:34] Carlos: about pilot — we want to try dedicated capacity for a month to see cost and latency gains. what does onboarding look like?
[03:40] Jordan: typical pilot: 2-4 week setup to provision a small dedicated pool, model onboarding (we can bring your existing open model or use our curated variant), run synthetic and real traffic benchmarks, then 2-4 week observation window. paperwork: simple reserved commit for pilot, and an MSA addendum if you need private deployment.
[03:57] Maya: timeline-wise, we want results before end of q1. that fits.
[04:00] Samira: i'll propose a concrete benchmark plan: 1) 95/99 p latency runs at 1x and 3x concurrency; 2) cache miss/hit profile capture; 3) cost per 1M tokens comparison across hosted, quantized, and dedicated.
[04:13] Carlos: sounds good. what about model versions — we need deterministic rollouts and rollback.
[04:18] Samira: rollout support for version pinning, canary, A/B and automatic fallback to safe model variant if an invocation fails. we'll document the exact flags.
[04:25] Anita: for the SOC auditor we also need who has access to logs in Redwood org, RBAC details.
[04:30] Jordan: we'll send the RBAC matrix and the list of personnel that have access to customer logs.
[04:34] Maya: a couple of product asks: 1) better cost breakdown by route and model 2) historical usage sampling so we can forecast ramp 3) more granular token attribution per user session.
[04:45] Jordan: roadmap item 1 and 2 are underway in the console; we'll add your request for session-level attribution as an enhancement ticket.
[04:51] Leo: i'll file an enhancement and include you, maya, to capture the exact fields you need.
[04:55] Carlos: small nit — our devs found some mismatch in the SDK where the error code for model fallback is different from the docs; caused some confusion in our retry logic.
[05:03] Samira: thanks, we'll triage that; can you share the exact request/response? we'll get a patch out.
[05:08] Maya: OK last thing on costs — can you show a worked example of how batching + quantization would affect our spend for the search workload?
[05:16] Jordan: yes — i'll include model-specific examples in the pricing deck. quick rule of thumb: batching + dedicated reserve tends to be biggest single lever; quantization ~20-35% savings depending on model.
[05:27] Maya: great.
[05:28] Jordan: wrap up — next steps: i'll send pricing and pilot proposal; samira will run the benchmark; anita will share SOC2 contact and SSO metadata; leo will schedule pilot kickoff. any other items?
[05:40] Maya: no that's it, thanks everyone.
[05:41] Carlos: thanks.
[05:42] Jordan: thanks team; we'll follow up via email and calendar.

End of transcript. Links mentioned: incident postmortem: https://redwood.example/incidents/2026-11-05, pricing deck placeholder: https://redwood.example/decks/peregrine-pricing-q4
